title: Session/user root-span attributes are UC-only; the generic MLflow exporter reads them from TraceInfo metadata
answers: should session.id be added to all MLflow traces
where to set session and user attributes for TypeScript tracing
V3 trace search session user metadata vs span attributes
why not promote session to attributes in MlflowSpanProcessor
body:
Invariant: Session and user values are promoted to session.id / user.id root-span attributes only in the Unity Catalog path (DatabricksUCTableSpanProcessor). The generic MlflowSpanProcessor does not do this.
Enforced at: libs/typescript/core/src/exporters/mlflow.ts:MlflowSpanProcessor (a comment before updateTraceInfo states that V3 search reads user and session from TraceInfo metadata, and that only UC-backed V4 traces need root-span attributes).
What breaks if skipped: Adding the promotion to the generic processor changes span attributes for every V3 trace without being needed by search. Keep the promotion scoped to UC exports and leave session/user in traceMetadata for V3.
applies: Changes to TypeScript exporters that set session, user, or related metadata on traces or spans.
says: Trace viewer shows unnecessary session and user tags on standard exported spans.
Standard trace search should filter by user without altering span attributes.
Session and user fields are missing from root spans in Unity Catalog traces.
Filter traces by session in the tracking interface using trace metadata.
Keep session and user details in trace overview instead of span attributes.
search: In TypeScript trace exporters, session and user values are promoted to session.id and user.id root-span attributes only in DatabricksUCTableSpanProcessor for Unity Catalog exports. Generic MlflowSpanProcessor in libs/typescript/core/src/exporters/mlflow.ts must keep session and user data in TraceInfo metadata because standard V3 trace search reads metadata directly, while only UC-backed V4 traces require root-span attributes. Promoting these values in the generic processor unnecessarily alters span attributes across all standard V3 traces.
